notes: Read SKILL.md and all 82 files in references/ in full (addgene, alphafold, alphavantage, bea, bindingdb, biogrid, bls, brenda, cbioportal, census, chebi, chembl, clinicaltrials, clinpgx, clinvar, cod, cosmic, dailymed, database_selection_guide, datacommons, dbsnp, disgenet, drugbank, ecb, emdb, ena, encode, ensembl, epa, eurostat, fda, federal-reserve, fred, gene-ontology, geo, gnomad, gtex, gwas-catalog, hca, hpo, human-protein-atlas, interpro, jaspar, kegg, lincs-l1000, materials-project, metabolomics-workbench, monarch, mousemine, myvariant, nasa-exoplanet-archive, nasa, ncbi-gene, ncbi-protein, ncbi-taxonomy, nist, noaa, omim, opentargets, openweathermap, pdb, pride, pubchem, quickgo, reactome, regulomedb, retrieval-contract, rummageo, sdss, sec-edgar, simbad, sra, string, tcga-gdc, treasury, ucsc-genome, uniprot, usgs, uspto, who, worldbank, zinc). The skill turns a user's question into reproducible, provenance-tracked lookups against about 80 public or registered scientific, regulatory, financial and demographic database APIs, with one reference file of endpoints, parameters, pagination and pitfalls per database.

It has the agent run curl (or another HTTP client) through Bash against live third-party APIs (SKILL.md:163-170, opentargets.md:11-15, noaa.md:46-49). When a selected API needs a key, it checks one named environment variable silently (SKILL.md:152-155) and otherwise looks up only that key in .env (SKILL.md:108, 157; uspto.md:38). For BRENDA it tells the agent to write and run a Python script using the zeep SOAP library with the user's registered email and hashed password (brenda.md:3, 47-62, 82). It may save large raw outputs to a local file (SKILL.md:253). Medium risk because real credentials go to live services and code is generated and run. This is acceptable because the skill limits credential use to the single key the current request needs, forbids printing keys, auth headers, signed URLs or .env contents (SKILL.md:106-110, retrieval-contract.md:101), asks for confirmation before more than 10,000 records or 100 API calls (SKILL.md:28, 178), and treats API responses as untrusted data that must never go into shell commands or be followed as instructions (SKILL.md:30, 180-190; retrieval-contract.md:95-104; simbad.md:399-405).

Users should know: (1) SKILL.md:384-399 tells the agent to add a citation to the K-Dense paper in any manuscript, report, presentation or code release the skill materially contributed to, to tell the user it did so, and to fetch arxiv.org/export.arxiv.org first to confirm the reference. This is self-promotion that edits the user's deliverables, but it is disclosed and not hidden. (2) SEC EDGAR requires a User-Agent header with a name and email (sec-edgar.md:13-17), so the agent may need the user's contact details. (3) User query terms are sent to third-party services. (4) Several sources are paid or licensed (DrugBank, COSMIC, DisGeNET, Addgene, OMIM, Alpha Vantage premium), and the skill points to free alternatives. (5) Optional pointers to a separate `gget` skill (retrieval-contract.md:30, database_selection_guide.md:90, 109) are not required for the skill to work. (6) The signalled missing path `references/<database-name>.md` (SKILL.md:259) is a template for adding new databases, not a missing file. (7) BRENDA needs the zeep Python package and SRA FASTQ downloads need SRA Toolkit (sra.md:150). Neither is bundled, and the skill gives no install command for either.
